avis: fastfood qui s'apparente à une slowfood, réactivité que cela soit en salle ou au drive proche du néant peu importe l'heure

adresse: Gare SNCF Lille Flandres Rue de Tournai 59000 Lille
avis:
While the layout of this McDonald's is a bit wonky, it is very convenient to passengers transiting in Lille.

There is no easy place to wait for food, and you have to fight through the crowd to get to the tables.

The restroom, like many in Europe, are not very clean.

The servers who waited on me were very patient as I practiced my broken French. They do an excellent job handling lots of customers in a somewhat cramped space.

It was honestly fine. We expected better quality than American Mcdonald's and were unfortunately disappointed. They definitely put more effort into the presentation of their food which we appreciated. I also got a chocolate brownie macaroon which was delicious so that was a pleasant surprise. The girl I was with got an oreo mcflurry and it was just vanilla ice cream with oreo toppings which was not what we expected. Fine for a Mcdonald's

adresse: Route de l'Espiguette 30240 Le Grau du Roi
Centre Commercial Intermarché 37 rue Aubépin 30540 Milhaud

avis: This restaurant is dirty and there was a live mouse under the table which we noticed as we were leaving. The service was also slow. Avoid this place.

This location is a -100. My first time in Paris and I stopped by another McDonalds and grabbed a simple large potatoes; after midnight; they were hot and fresh.

This location is right outside my hotel and the first time I went there, my potatoes were cold. I went back another day and the entire interaction was weird. I ordered at the kiosk and somehow I wasn't charged but I saw my ticket come up and the light skinned black girl balled it up. I don't know their processes so I didn't say anything. I continued to wait and wait then I finally spoke up and another black girl said I still needed to pay. Like I said, I was confused because the 2 times prior the payment went through at the kiosk. I paid and my food came out. I walked a minute to the hotel and again the potatoes are cold and old. Mind you I saw new ones put down which is why I didn't bother to check before leaving. This time I decided to go back because why keep wasting money. I walked in and explained my food was cold and I wanted fresh fries. The cashier goes to another girl telling her my request and I don't need to understand the language to know they had an issue. A short bigger bodied woman comes up; never saying a word and I request new potatoes and tell her my food was cold yesterday as well. She takes the bag and with the ugliest attitude rolls her eyes and walks away and dumps the fries in a container. I am of course appalled. The fry guy adds more fries to the bag and she brings them over.

The whole establishment is rude and ghetto. Would not recommend. As an owner you should really review the staff you have in place here.
This location is in a very busy part of central Paris, so the extra star is for the very fast service you'll get here.

Very poor hygienic handling, no fork or knife, fries premade for 15 min and kept in the box.

Stay away

Okay, so it might seem weird that I'm reviewing a random McDonald's in Paris, but hear me out.

My friends and I took the Eurostar from London to Paris and when we finally got to our flat - which was right up the street - it was almost midnight and everything else was closed. So, we decided to stop here to pick up dinner. I was a little confused with the kiosks that you use to place your order, but I appreciated it because I was able to correctly place my order without worrying that the employee understood me correctly. They also offered nutritional and allergy information, so I could make sure there was no dairy in my meal.

After placing my order my food came out and was fresh. Surprisingly, it taste better than American McDonald's. Well, maybe not surprisingly.

I recommend this McDonald's if you're in the area and need something on the cheap side to eat. It definitely wasn't extremely cheap, like in the States, but if you're looking for something familiar than this is the perfect place to stop.

I usually don't post reviews for chain restaurants, but here I am making an exception for McDonald's in France. Food is pretty much like ordinary McDonald's fast food here in the US with basically the only difference is a few menu items (like potato wedges, ice cream in a tube and sorbet) and McCafe bakeries, so I'm not complaining about food. I actually went to few McDonald's locations while I was in Paris and I had some issues with payment at almost all of them I went to, except for the one on the Champs-Elysées. I go to the kiosk and place my order and attempt to pay there with my debit card. About 5 or 6 times, my payment card "declined" because of it not being "debited"(according to what said on the touch screen) when my card was a DEBIT card. The final time, a receipt prints just for me to take to the cashier and PAY AGAIN at the register. Payment finally goes through at the register and I receive my food. Next thing I know, I check my bank account summary and I see about 5 or 6 charges of the same amount from Mc Donald's. I filed a claim for those unauthorized charges and got my money back, but Mc Donald's France really needs to fix their payment systems on their kiosks. This review wasn't aiming towards one location as it happened to me when I went to a few, so this same review will be posted on a few Mc Donald's France yelp pages.

FREE WIFI!!! Thats why my friends and I were here. We got food and I got a frappe and it was typical McDonalds.

We were gonna use its bathroom there (on break of our tour) but decided to use the bathroom in Starbucks across from McDonalds instead. But the free wifi is very convenient!!!

I take no pleasure in going scorched Earth on any business, but it cannot be avoided for this particular McDonald's location.

Let me preamble this review by saying that the manager, a gentleman, who wore a white short sleeve dress shirt and black vest on the Monday evening (April 6, 2026) that we dined here is an utter despicable person - and possibly some members of his staff too. Due to multiple incidents during our visit, my wife and I felt that their actions seemed to have some racial undertones during our dine-in experience.

Firstly, I took a photo of their McDonald's counter from afar inside of the mall and the manager noticed me and immediately rushed around the counter and got into my face aggressively. He tried to intimidate me by asking, in a menacing manner, why I took the photo, repeatedly. I informed him that I was just using it to write a food review and he DEMANDED that I delete it immediately. I informed him that it was just a picture of their McDonald's and that he was not in the photo.

His request puzzled me, but since I didn't feel like starting a war between our countries over such a small issue, I obliged to de-escalate, but the fact that he was so aggressive about it and even stood over me to watch me empty my phone trash like a child absolutely ticked me off. His aggression and attitude towards the matter was uncalled for. He could have requested it nicely, but it took it a different direction. (I took another photo of their McDonald's from a different angle anyway).

Second, my wife went over to the counter to request for kids meal toys because they forgot it in our order. She observed that he happily helped another customer, of a different race, with a forgotten item, but when they made eye contact, he walked away from her and sent another employee over and didn't help her. She stated that he clearly noticed her and just decided not to help her himself. Besides that, we observed another family of Asian descent seemingly disrespected by another staff member when the staffer kind of just dumped their order at their table in an odd/disrespectful way.

I tried looking for this manager after my wife's incident, so that I could confront him, but he disappeared for a good hour until we were leaving with our kids.

Not that I needed the aggravation to pan their food, but it was absolutely the worst McDonald's food we everrrrrr had. Despite the experience, we were hoping to enjoy our food, but it was utterly not edible. I don't have McD often, but I enjoyed it everytime I've had it...until now, so here goes my actual review.

THE FOOD
----------------
- ALL of the food was absolutely abysmal here.
- Steak burger was so well-done that I'm pretty sure it reincarnated in cow heaven.
- Chicken bacon onion sandwich was rather disgusting and just full of lettuce.
- Kids Filet-o-fish was definitely the worst we ever had. All it had in there was a smidge of ketchup. It was as sad as anything I've ever seen.
- Fries were cold when they arrived. Don't think I have ever experienced that at ANY McD's in the states.

THE SERVICE
-------------------
- Do I need to elaborate any further?

THE SURROUNDINGS
------------------------------------
+ There are lots of tables and seats in the food court for this McD's. One (and the ONLY) bright side of dining here.

RANDOM OBSERVATIONS
--------------------------------------
- Said my piece above.

- Located in the food court right after exiting the Louvre--convenient in theory, but that's about the only positive
- Several self-order kiosks were out of service, which led to long lines; the whole process felt rushed and chaotic
- The dining area was bright but noticeably unclean, with sticky tables; seating is spaced well apart so it would be comfortable if cleaned properly
- Ordering is done at the kiosk--take a number and find a seat while food is brought out, but the process felt disorganized; servers wandered around with trays of food, clearly struggling to locate the correct parties
- Service was extremely rude and dismissive; our order was missing items, and when I tried to ask about it, a male staff member (who seemed like a manager) ignored me after making eye contact and appeared to pass me off to someone else--this right after he had helped another customer; the interaction felt uncomfortable and disrespectful
- I was directed to the McCafé counter to resolve the issue, where a female employee was noticeably more friendly and helpful
- Our Happy Meals were missing the toys and didn't even come in the proper packaging, while other customers clearly received theirs correctly.
- Food was shockingly bad for the price--burgers were overcooked and drier than jerky, the chicken sandwich tasted worse than cardboard, and the fries were cold; the only thing the kids would touch was a packaged strawberry yogurt drink
- We were given just two napkins for a meal for four, which pretty much sums up the lack of care across the board

At the Louvre mall food court:
Big Mac- bread was hard, sauce was light
Fries- soggy and cold
Hold your craving until you get back to the States.
Find a better French alternative while you travel.
I should have!

Service is too slow and the order was delivered incomplete in more ways than originally thought possible. It's also the kind of place that engages in stubborn unhelpfulness and lack of accountability. If you wait in a queue for help retrieving missing items, you are told to see a manager. If you then ask the manager for help, he may tell you to use the queue.

Would not fall into this tourist trap again. Beware.

Great service, stop by for expresso coffee.
Very nice and clean, II really enjoyed my dine.

I don't know why there are so many bad reviews for this McDonalds. Let me just be clear if you are from the US like I am McDonald's in France are far better than the McD's in the states. Better food across the board at their restaurants. You order and pay at the kiosks unless you are paying with cash then you order on the kiosk and pay at the register. I was there for the Royal with Cheese IYKTYK, my son got two cheeseburgers and my daughter got french fries. It was a tad overpriced. We enjoyed everything we received. It was made fast and correct we took it to go. I would go back when in France and had a hankering for McD's.

The kiosks were confusing. Then you take the receipt it spits out to the counter to pay and then wait on a separate line to pick up the food. Whole process took 30min. The food at least tasted pretty much the same as in the States.
Per usual for Europe this McDonalds does not disappoint! The establishment is professional staff, clean establishment, fresh hot food, and bathrooms you can actually use for one euro.

One of the worst McDonalds in Paris. You can't be expecting more if you are eating at McDonalds but this place is awful. Usually Micky D's would be 2-3 stars but this deserves negative stars.

May it's a tourist place they don't care about customers but we pay for our food. Ambiance is good as it is Tuesday and the Louvre is closed, very very less people, but mam they didn't leave room to disappoint us. Please help yourself somewhere else to eat.

McDonalds

This is only a review of their macarons. Yes, I went to McDonalds for mararons.

I have no idea why going to "McDo" (that's what the Frenchies call it) is better in Paris than in Topeka, but it just is. We had just bought a half dozen macarons at the fancy bakery Bechu (see my review). We just arrived in Paris and I wanted to take my 10 year old daughter on a stroll to see how the natives behave in their natural habitat. I asked a street vendor about the best bakery in the neighborhood and Voilà, we found Bechu. We bought a half a dozen beautiful looking macarons at Bechu and then I spotted the McDo across the street. I heard that they sold macarons so we went in and found a nice selection of 8 macarons. They packaged them in a cute little McCafé box. In the interests of scientific research, we did a side by side blind tasting at home. McDo won, although the Bechu macarons were also excellent. I highly recommend you do your own taste test.
Service is awful, was waiting over 10 minutes for my food and when I finally received the food it was cold! Staff were very rude when I brought up and wouldn't exchange it.

If I could give this negative stars I would. Friend got extremely sick after eating McDonald's. Now a few days have passed since and catches tonsillitis. Fast forward to today, it's not tonsillitis anymore and they don't know what it is. It all started when she ate that burger in this dirty ass restaurant. DO NOT RECOMMEND!
Junk food is all they have there.even the salads taste like crap.nothing is healthy.if you have all these great restaurants around you why go to McDonald's.

As an American, I'd say 100% not worth trying the Mickey D's in Paris. There was nothing special or unique about it, aside from location.

If you're interested in paying double for below average fast food, go for it.
Otherwise, I'd suggest the local fast fooderies, or trying anything else.

Used the touchscreens at entrance. Cards were not accepted, then paid at front cashier. Have noticed that the bill has been charged three times. Do not use touch screens, there were several people having problems.

Expensive for McDonald's

I always visit a McDonald's whenever I travel. But I was not impressed with the McDonald's in Paris. I chose this one out of convenience - it was the closest one to my Airbnb.

I was grateful that there were self ordering stations with English because I do not know any French. I struggle when getting my order because they called out numbers in French.. and again, I don't know French.

Above all, I was disappointed in their sorbet served in a waffle cone. I actually didn't know I was ordering a sorbet... I thought it was a red velvet ice cream, but it was some fruity sorbet that tasted very fake.

--
taste / 1
aesthetics / 1
vibe / 2
service / 3
price for quality / 1
OVERALL / 1.6

This was probably the 3rd McDonald's we tried in Paris.
We dined in around 10am, it wasn't crowded in the morning compared to the afternoons.
At the other McDonald's in the afternoon and dinner gets super crowded, like it's hard to find a place to sit down.
We self ordered on the kiosk.
The food tasted good as in there's no greasy aftertaste.
When browsing the menu I saw that they also sold Macarons and Mcbaguette.

Disappointed with my visit. The food came out cold, and there was no option for a soda refill. For the prices they charge, basic quality and service should be a given. Definitely not the experience I expected

I was hesitant to review this because I only ordered an ice tea while I waited for my train.

Although it was a great meeting point when I had to regroup with my parents.

Accessible and fast wifi, clean, easy to spot, it's not the worst Mcdonald's I've been to.

This McD's has terrible sandwiches and unhelpful staff. I would suggest
giving the money to a homeless and saving the calories. Not worth your visit!

This is the worse experience I ever had in Mcdonald. I was a big fan in USA, but for sure not in Paris. I wanted to order coffee after I used restroom. However, it required codes, and I was about to go upstair to order a coffee. A middle east guy put the code and told me that I can use restroom, when I was using restroom, he was bothering my husband to ask for money. I was like WTF, and the restroom was in downstair, and we were kind of scared. I just pull out 70 cents and ran. I will never ever walk in to Mcdonald Paris anymore


FYI, the toilet has no seat, has no water to wash my hands. I had to use alcohol wash. I was basically running out this place, because it was so creepy. What's wrong with Mcdonald in Paris?

I came to Paris for fine french cuisine. Gordon Ramsey said on kitchen nightmares that french cuisine is the best cuisine. Seeing as Sir Ramsey's word is biblical in the culinary world, I trusted him. Lo and behold my reward is what I can only describe as worse than 8 day old leftovers cooked by my donkey of a sister.

The food was heavily salted and high in saturated fats -- Certainly not a la carte.

The service was sub par. Nobody came to take my order so I had to get up out of my chair and ask myself. I didn't even have my hover board with me. I had to walk!

The food came promptly. This is where they earned their two stars. I didn't think it was possible to cook food in 15 seconds but they must have some masterful french chefs back there.

'La cheeseburger'

For my first dish I was anticipating some sort of blu cheese dressed steak. Perhaps fillet mignon. The woman squinted at me when I asked for it medium rare. This did make me suspicious. However, when I was crudely given some sort of cardboard clad ground horsemeat and maize I was disgusted. After the first bite I spat it out and threw the steak at the manager. It was drenched in mustard and pickles. Certainly not appropriate dressing for a fine steak.

For my next dish I received what I suspected to be escargot. However they turned out to be 4 measly chicken nuggets. They didn't even give me any sauce. What was I supposed to dip them in? I ate the first two and then threw the rest at the pigeons outside. Perhaps that was cruel, they are accustomed to higher standards of breading.


I left before proceeding to the next course. I had seen enough. Gordon Ramsey you have lost my respect.

France you are here by dismantled as the worlds food capital.

There;s nothing like walking along a Paris road wanting a fast bite for lunch, than to come across a Paris McDonald.... Kind of weird, you go in find what is a vending, punch in your meal order, walk over to another section and pickup your food which is ready with a couple of minutes... Fast, efficient and painless... Their lunch meal is a bit different than the US. Ours came with fries, drink, large sandwich, and another smaller sandwich, for about 9 Euro.

The Good.

-There's free wi-fi.
-There's a bathroom.
-You don't have to buy any food to take advantage of the previous two items.
-The Royale with Cheese is a real thing. Nice to have confirmation.

The Bad.

-The food, I'm assuming.

The Ugly.

-I feel like a freeloader for using their wi-fi/bathroom. Probably because I am.

Came here for a second time today. First time was yesterday. My kids were missing American food so we brought them here. We were pleasantly surprised that the food tasted exactly the same! Big Mac was just as good as were the chicken nuggets and fries. Knocked off a star as both times our drinks were not filled to the top nor were our fries.

After walking through tons of debris to get to Mcdonalds we had some high hopes. However The burgers taste like cardboard. I bet it would still be preserved in 15 years. The drunks were friendly, and service was quick which is not surprising because the food was probably out for years.

paris is expensive for a broke, cheap ass traveler such as myself. The last thing I care about when over seas is sampling their exotic food cause have you ever had the squirts in another country?

Yeah, bathrooms and pepto arent the easiest things to fin when you cant speak or understand the language!

Either way it was about the same as mcdonalds here except when I went 3 years ago, they were already serving fruit.

I got the Royale with cheese and a coke. Nothing better or worse then here in the states.

Very clean place. You order from a screen at all of the American fast foods probably because the computer has so many stored languages. You just wait in the take home line. They put French onions on the burgers which is a lil weird, but it tastes similar to an American burger.

Traveled to paris, fr during the late 90's and i ate quite a few meals at mcdonalds in the area. Why you ask? Well my french was very limited not wanting to see if poison or poisson would be served me based on my pronunciation. Besides picking up un, der, twa, cat ... Was pretty easy and thank god for the photos so i get an idea what i was ordering. Also the fact prices relative to the cafes were more in line with what i was willing to spend.
As for the menu i actually ate alot of chicken on this trip because of the mad cow scare. I dont recall any unique french twists to the mcdonalds here unlike china where there was no apple pie but taro root pie instead.
As for the whole setup with ordering food its just like any other mcdonalds in the states.

Upon entering "McDonald's", I had very high hopes; many of my friends have eaten at the restaurant before and I have noticed the place referenced in a few films, documentaries, radio broadcasts, etc. However, after overlooking the somewhat cheap and childish façade (they really should have settled on a more sombre tone of red and yellow in order to establish a more serious tone for their clientele's dining experience), I made my way through the rather heavy doors and into the atrium.

This is when my opinion of the place started to crumble. As I stood, waiting for the maître d' to escort me to my table, I briefly scanned the entirety of the restaurant's interior: 'dated' to say the least. The walls were bare, the floors were covered with cheap tiles and on these tiles, I routinely saw squished fries, abandoned napkins and other general refuse that would have been much better suited to the seemingly abundant waste disposal bins rather than the floor of the restaurant. It was quite frankly an appalling first impression of the place. What is more, the maître d' never arrived and I was left simply standing in the mouth of the doorway. This had clearly irked other customers as everyone had abandoned usual practice of waiting to be seated and had taken the task of finding a table into their own hands. The restaurant had not managed to make a good first impression, nevertheless, determined to give the place a fair shot, I made my way to a vacant table.

The service in the place leaves a lot to be desired. Just as the maître d' had failed to make himself known to the customers, so did all the waiting staff. Yet again, diners were forced to take matters into their own hands and approach the kitchen, ordering their food at the serving station, paying on the spot, presumably so as to guarantee that their meals arrive, stemming from the broken trust between them and the restaurant caused by the lack of staff presence in the front-of-house. I followed suite and placed my order. I selected their "Chicken McNuggets" to start, followed by the "Big Mack" accompanied by "French Fries" as my main course, rounded off by a "McFlurry Ice Cream Sundae" for dessert. I refrained from ordering a beverage given the distinct lack of choice. If you only drunk sparkling sodas then you would have no problems, however there were no decent wines or other appropriate supper-drinks on the menu. Therefore, in my slightly irritated state, I decided against ordering a drink. To my surprise, the "Chicken McNuggets" were delivered to me on the spot, merely seconds after paying my rather reasonable bill (I didn't include a tip, the staff didn't warrant it. You could see others had shared the same thought as their large, plastic tip jar adjacent to the till contained only copper coins). At least they were able to offer rather rapid service, although it made me question the effort and dedication that would have been put into the preparation of my food.

I picked up my serving plateau (waiters were still nowhere to be seen) and turned to head back to my table, though before I could make my move, my "Big Mack" and "French Fries" were hastily dumped onto the plateau... At the same time as the starter! I assumed this must have been a mistake as I had barely had enough time to verify that I had the correct amount of "Chicken McNuggets" (6), let alone finish them. I gestured to get the attention of an employee and thankfully, my gaze was met with a pair of apologetic eyes. I was relieved and waited for the becapped employee to take back my premature main course. However my shock was only increased exponentially when my "McFlurry Ice Cream Sundae" was placed on the plateau too. Before I could say anything, they employee was already having an interaction with the customer behind me. Fed up, I gathered the serving plateau and headed back to the table.

The food left a lot to be desired. It was extremely salty, heavy with the grease and was certainly prepared using largely frozen or otherwise-preserved ingredients. By this time I knew that "McDonald's" had failed to impress me and I did not understand why it had garnered such widespread public revere (it has been featured in over 3 national newspaper articles). I wiped by lubricated fingers on the plastic wrapping that shrouded my "Big Mack" hamburger, a wrapping which also served as my plate, and left. The dishwashing team had clearly lost control of their crockery amidst the swarming mob of customers who were all ordering at the same time, forcing the kitchen to include these plastic wrappings as some sort of surface for the food to be eaten from.

Overall, "McDonald's" can be described in one word: rushed. The décor looks like it was rushed during the building of the place, the training of the staff must have been rushed, the preparation of the food was rushed and, as a result of the generally negative experience, I made sure my experience in there was rushed; I couldn't get out quickly enough.

It's McDonalds sure. This location is near many hotels, including the one we were at, so we called in for some late-nite grub a couple nights. You also can get a beer here with your meal, which is pretty cool.

The staff appeared to be a little overwhelmed around 4 PM on a weekday compared to the amount of people waiting on their orders. The lobby area was absolutely packed and people were waiting on the self-order machines. There were tables available, but not all had been cleaned off as a result of the overwhelmed staff. Food was fine - what you'd expect from McDonald's.

Visiting a McD on travels is a must. So I came to see what are the differences between North America McD and Paris McD. Well they have ice cream (that tasted like gelato) in waffle cones (strawberry, chocolate and vanilla flavors). On top their cafe options/items list is huge. You can get macaroons here.

B and I both got the strawberry waffle cone. It was ok. I would prefer it if it had a strong milk flavor to it or that it doesn't tasted so much like a gelato.

The McD decor is not the traditional yellow, white and red walls and tables (like the ones in North America). It is somewhat fancier than the NA locations or the other McDs that I have been to.

Also the McD in Paris has a point system. If you buy enough from McD, you can use your points to redeem food.

We have gone from the absolute worst McDonalds (Versailles) to one of the most pleasant. Although it is extremely busy as it's next to the Jardin des Plantes (and all it's children), service was fast and efficient and everyone was wished a "Bon Appetit" with a smile as we picked up our order.

As an aside, it's sad to say that this is the third McDonalds we've visited in France. As soon as our kid sees those Golden Arches all hope is lost. Sigh...

It's hard to remember what the facts are when it comes to childhood memories, but I am sure my family didn't have McDonald's often -- and when we did, it was part-treat part-parent-exhaustion.

So what is the draw of going to McDonald's in another country? I don't know, maybe it is the newness of the menu, or the desire for a new look at memories.

You can't go to McDonald's and not order fries. Here, it was limp as the lost leg of an octopus. I had heard about the Croque McDo from friends -- a fast food take on croque monsieur -- and I had expected a large sandwich. Instead, it was a flat, palm-sized snack that was delicious, but not filling.

The CBO and 280 Moutarde (both square shaped!) seemed intriguing, so I ordered those too. I didn't like the 280 very much. It was dry, dense, and tasted like five-minute old mustard-flavored gum. But the CBO was decent, and I can't say anything good or bad about it.

This McDonald's seemed spacious and filled with young and old people with arms slung around each other, on dates. It was quite a very different experience from McDonald's across the United States.

chill but hella people during meet's hours, good service and accuracy
purchase terminals available for simplicity, they can ask if you have ID MacDo or not, terminals can accept different means of payment

Waited so long even though there were no people. And when I came home the burger was too old. The salat is brown, and the chicken in my mc chicken was so hard you could feel it was more than a day old. Not okay.....
Nice McDonald's with English speaking manager. The typical set up and the place is clean.

I'm one of those people who very much enjoys trying McDonald's around the world. Think you're better than me all you want, but I grew up with McDonald's being such a special treat, and I still love it. Hmph! :P

Now the McDonald's in Marseille, France DELIVERS on unique items we don't have in the United States.
A mini fries in a cute plastic container was my favorite part of it all!
But from a chocolate sandwich (not the best, lol) to a croque monsieur (solid) to different sauces for the chicken nuggies - I was loving experiencing all the food McDonald's had to offer.

Now, we get into the nitty gritty of this location. The good is that you can order from their computerized screen and have little to no interaction with staff. This location is in a very busy area, and they do not keep up with the cleaning in the restaurant. And I'll just say, the bathroom was abysmal.

Now the positive of this location is that it's two stories and there are counter seats looking out the window on the second floor. As a tourist, I really loved being able to look out and people watch, see the ocean and just feel like I wasn't at a McDonald's which eating my very bizzare, thick, nutty chocolate smashed between two buns.

adresse: Angle rue Pierre Terrasse Rue Louis Pasteur 69300 Caluire-et-Cuire

avis: Nice big location with lots of seating outside and the second floor. The staff are friendly and the food was served quickly at the table.

Was charged on my debit card 46.00 of food for this restaurant and they did not have the card, just the numbers. I was in Texas at the time and I live in Minnesota. How does that restaurant let that happen. IF YOU MUST eat there use currency ONLY

adresse: Avenue Jean Jaures Centre commercial Atac ZAC Le Clos Racine 27600 Gaillon

avis: We poked our heads into this McDonald's out of curiosity. It's housed in the oldest building in Rouen we were told, but you could hardly tell as it is modernized and snazzy both inside and outside. It's a quite cozy and comfortable McDonald's, and kudos, good for them!

It is, of course, an interesting juxtaposition to find a McDonald's/McCafe in the shadow of Rouen's Gros Horloge. But this is a good location for the visitor to Rouen. There are two service counters, one for the standard food menu and one for the McCafe menu. The McCafe serves French macarons! The are quite tasty.

Customers may place an orders at a of bank self-service machines. They will guide you in several languages. Pick up and pay at the counters. Keep your receipt as it includes the restroom entry code. Two floors of seating. A nice spot for quick refreshment when visiting historic Rouen.

Everything was closed...this is what sucks about Paris. It's hard to find places that stay open pass 9 pm. So Frenchie went out and got something from McDonalds - I can't remember what I tried here, but I just remember they had a few things that we don't have in the states.

Not a fan but hey if you're desperate...I guess this will suffice.

Late night craving of McDonald's even in Paris. This restaurant was cleaner than most and the staff was helpful. Three minute walk from hotel and two minutes from metro.

I ordered a coffee and a pastry and it took almost 45 minutes. We just gave up, we walked up to the desk 5 times and every time they told us to go to the cafe or it would be out within five minutes. The cafe had no one behind the table. Really ridiculous, I would not recommend coming here. Total waste of time and we didn't even get our coffee

It's actually really great,the food was good,except there was really really disrespectful customers,they were laughing and giggling behind my back,and I have no idea who they are,because I'm not French and I don't understand anything. In general,nice McDonald's,but not very clean

Super Busy McDonalds between two tram stops. There is a self-service order kiosk that allows you to bypass the line and order in your choice of many languages and pay by credit card! Really good stuff. Then just go pick up your order at the pick-up window. Super easy!

It's definitely a popular location to get food. With the automated ordering kiosks and a separate section for pastries and desserts, the looks is more like a European patisserie or bakery. Food is certainly not as inexpensive as American McDonalds but you can get a decent breakfast combo for about 3.50 Euro a person. They have a few options. Dinner is a little pricier. If you're an American and never been to Europe before, don't expect coffee sizes to be even adequate compared to what you're used to back home and don't expect amazing service that's expected in a fast food place. Most of the coffee is a lot of expressos served in small cups that might seem a little expensive compared to what you get in America.

The European culture especially here in France is that people like to take their time, not be rushed, and things go a lot slower. This placed tends to get packed during dinner hours and you see a lot of French youth packing the place and the staff struggling to keep pace. My recommendation is that if you live close to this location that it's good for breakfast when it opens at 7:30. Especially if you don't want to go to local French pastry places for breakfast if they don't serve egg and all that. Dinner is when you should go explore the city and take in the local places whether it's native French cuisine or any other cuisine and for the price and chance of it being packed, you're better off going elsewhere and walking around for your dinner. Here it depends on the location and the person taking your order (if they speak English fluently or not) to understand what your needs are. It's not the best McDonalds I've been to but it's not far from what I expect from an European and international location.

Horrible, just horrible. First, I get there. NO. AC. AT. ALL. It was literally 97 degrees out, and they also had the doors open, which made it worse. Started to order, fries, nuggets, a drink, the usual. Oh, and a thing to note, I ordered on the smart-order pad. So, I ordered, well I tried too. Had to order again and again, in total three times because the pad literally said "Error" each time I tried to order. It finally let me ordered and it gave me a ticket? I waited 30 minutes before realizing I had to give the ticket to a worker for the order to go through, which was really dumb as I thought the order would've already been ordered the second I paid for it and it gave no instruction once so ever that I had to give the ticket to the workers. Then, once I finally got my order in, I waited 45 more minutes for my food. Other people that just ordered got their food in no less than 5 minutes while me, who's waited over an hour and a half, still hasn't gotten his food! Seriously, what is this service? Finally, the food came out. Now, there was still one small problem, it was seating. Downstairs, no seating. Upstairs, no seating. Luckily, a family had just been finishing up and was leaving once I got upstairs, so now I could finally have some seating. I opened up the food, very disappointing. The drink had no ice and was barely cold, the nuggets tasted horrible, and fries had no salt while being incredibly soggy. Overall this place was a dump. If you hate bad food, horrible ambience, and slow service then DON'T go here. But, if you would like a horrendous, sickening, and awful experience, you might like this place! :D

Awful... over 30 minutes for an order. Won't take orders at a register so you can't customize an order (I can't eat onions). If I wasn't so sick and want comfort food I would never come in here.
Update.... Waited 40 minutes and the order is wrong, fries- which I thought would be perfect have been sitting for awhile. - awful

I went there for breakfast around 8 am on a Tuesday morning. There was one other person in front of me, and once she was done the girl behind the counter took and fulfilled my order (two coffees) quickly. Unfortunately, there was none of the breakfast sandwiches (McMuffins) I was hoping for, only pastries were offered, and the "burger" section hadn't opened yet.

Great McDonald's,yummy food,good service, BUT, the floor is super slippery and that made me trip and fall and cause the chair to fall nearly onto me. The staff helped me,they asked me something,but I had no idea what they said so I just nodded and walked off awkwardly. The toilets are nice,but the code had me confused. If you want a nice meal,go there
Waited 20 minutes for an ice cream and never got it. Ignored by staff when I asked why I didn't get it yet. No wonder this McDonald's has so many 1 star reviews.

I didn't think it was possible to make the McDonald's chain in The States look good, but you people pulled it off.

I went here because the menu was more expansive and pretty much as a goof- a New Yorker in France eating at Mickey D's did make for a funny Instagram post.

But the laughs stopped there.

No one would explain that I had to use the automated system, pay a cashier, then wait- that one is my bad. After all,I'm in a foreign country.

My # comes up,I go to the counter.

'We ran out,so we gave you this wrap instead.'

Go upstairs, wife goes in bathroom- tampons and excrement the floor.

Bun was burnt (?!), fries were saturated in grease and undercooked. The ONE thing I thought the French would improve upon (McDonald's in the States has great fries), was inedible.
The wrap, my wife picked at and tossed. Burger was like in the ststesr,except they don't burn the bun there.

avis: I know it is really weird to review a McDonald's (especially in France). I generally abhor McDonald's in the US. However, this particular one saved my life since the apartment I'm currently staying in does not have wi-fi. McDonald's has 100% free wi-fi. Not only that, I actually ate a burger! It was not at all like the US burgers. This was closer to a burger one might get at a decent diner in New Jersey. The fries were excellent. The coffee is French--it is good. It is so funny to see macarons at a McDonald's. This one is especially clean and comfortable. The bathrooms are well maintained. You actually need a code to get in (look at the bottom of your receipt after making a purchase). I amazingly recommend this McDonald's.
Good location. Very clean. Nice service. Our burgers were great, nice and hot!! Large seating area.

Came here with my girlfriend as we needed wifi and a rest from travelling with our luggage. around Bordeaux, surprised to find that McDonalds here doesn't open until 10am on Sunday but fair enough, We're British an American, we're used to fast food being shovelled in our mouths 24/7. A few locals tried to enter before 10am too however.

This place didn't bother opening on time and no one seemed too fussed. The food itself took forever to materialise and there was a lot of people waiting around for their orders too. Again, the staff didn't seem too fazed, they were still getting things together, as if they just turned up a few minutes ago. .

We finally got our order which was somehow cold despite the fact we ordered out food first. Our table was also dirty and hadn't been cleaned. To cap it all off, the food also gave me the shits.

Is it pointless reviewing a Mcdonald's? Probably but it's a reminder to myself not to eat this crap.

It's a typical Mickey D's but with different hours than we are used to in the US. Check before you go or try to order online. Your US app doesn't work in France. We put the French app on our phone and it worked.

I have to admit... I love eating fast food once in a while (I try to limit my intake to 3-4 times per year tops!). If you are reading this review in English, chances are you are not from Bordeaux, let alone France! So remember "Pulp Fiction": a Royal with cheese here is a quarter pounder with cheese back home!! Enjoy!

avis:
This McDonald's is unlike any I've visited before. Yes, it has the usual counter with all the classic McDonald's items, but the real surprise is the mini bakery tucked inside. They offer cheesecake, macarons, cupcakes, muffins, donuts, cookies, and a full lineup of espresso drinks, cappuccinos, and specialty coffees. It feels almost like a café and a fast‑food spot merged into one.

The menu also goes beyond the standard McDonald's lineup. You'll find items like micro‑veggie mixes, Big Tasty Steak, Double Fish, Extreme Steak, and other regional specialties you won't see in most countries.

One thing to know: you need to make a purchase to use the bathroom, and they give you a token to access it. It's a bit unusual, but pretty common for busy tourist areas in Paris.

This place is not worthy of the beautiful street it's located on. When I placed my order I was given the option of having a drink with or without ice. I chose ice in the scorching heat. I received my drink without ice. This was just one of many things that were sub par. If a cookie cutter place like McDonald can't get it right its a sad thing.

It's McDonalds, what can you say

The beef is the men can pee for free, but the women have to cough up a Euro. REALLY???

Do better!!
Expect to pay to use the toilet. We stopped in for the loo and my kid wanted some French fries. It was interesting to see the different offerings.

This had to be the nicest and fanciest McDonald's in all of Paris. It was located very close to L'Arc de Triomphe on Av. des Champs-Élysées. I came in here to get some breakfast and to save some euros. It was very easy and convenient to place my order while using one of the many ordering kiosks. I ordered the brunch dejeuner: McMuffin egg & bacon, McMuffin bacon & beef, OJ, and espresso. I ordered a heartier meal as I anticipated a lot of walking for the rest of the day. The service and quality of the food was on par for any McDonald's that I'd visited all over the world. I used the relatively clean restroom before heading out. Unfortunately, they were out of soap so I had to use my own hand sanitizer.

We only went in to use the restroom, this place was packed! The women's room charged money to use, but the men's room was free to use. So, the women were smart, holding the door open as they exited for the next one entering.
Whatever do you do, don't take pics inside tho... the security guard (a.k.a. Photo natzi) will scream and yell at you! It's so odd that they don't permit photos inside, but they can't stop everyone, so what's the use in worrying about it?
McDonald's is a joke anyway, this location is no different than the others.

After a long day at the Eiffel Tower, wanted to get some lunch. I knew beforehand McDonalds in Paris, was nothing like we have back in the US. After dining here, that was surely confirmed.

Upon Entry, you run into the McCafe section, which in America, is basically apple pie and ice cream (which the machines rarely work) however here, they had a little of everything! I opted for a Big Mac, which did not come in the standard box, but tasted almost similar, but seemed fresh. The fries were almost the same and the cheesecake was pretty good here.

Another major difference was the quality in service. The employee spoke English, which seems to be a rarity here, and she seemed very happy to speak it. She was very helpful, didn't rush me and assisted me wonderfully.

Overall, I was very happy with my experience here!

In Paris and wanting a cup of coffee.....where do you go, McDonald's of course! Shocking how beautiful and clean (you could eat off the floors). The coffee was absolutely delicious. We don't eat fast food but I'm pretty sure it too is amazing.

I always stopped by a McDonald's when overseas and saw this streetside near a major tourist attraction Arc De Triomphe. As you walk in, the vibe is much different. The whole restaurant is organized, from a separate pastry, coffee bar to 15 touchscreens to order your food. Once you get your ticket, you will wait until they call your order. I have never seen such a major organization in the background, workers having specific roles, reducing multitasking that occurs at US McDonald's. The upstairs area is super clean. A worker stays up here and constantly sweeps floors and wipes tables quickly once someone leaves. The taste for the Big Mac is a bit different with the secret sauce. Overall, I had a pleasant time here, unlike the experiences in the States.

Maybe I loved this McDonald's because I was getting homesick and I just didn't find the right places to eat in Paris. This location is awesome. Back in the U.S. we have two or three dessert choices. This location had like 20! They had freaking canelles! The macarons were awesome! Not Pierre Hermé caliber but still darn good.
The burgers tasted like they would in the states but the crispy chicken actually tasted better than the chicken burgers we have here.
The coffee bar was awesome! I've never seen someone draw shots of espresso in California. The seating was nice and open. They had hip music going. The outside seating was so Parisian and beautiful. The location was beautiful, the people were nice and the food was YuMm-O. Loved seeing the different offerings in another country. If you're in Paris, stop by this location!
